quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Where does the first closure happen: at the lips or at the tongue tip?
quests.explanation: That was "pin": the lips closed and opened for the first sound. "Tin" opens with the tongue tip against the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lips versus tongue tip: the bilabial stop closes at the lips; the alveolar stop closes at the ridge behind the upper teeth. The vowel transitions into each differ slightly.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the lips for the bilabial stop; touch the tongue tip to the ridge for the alveolar stop.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are breathy stops. Listen to which part of the mouth releases.
quests.explanation: "Tie" is released by the tongue tip, giving a brighter click. "Pie" is released by the lips and sounds fuller.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The two stops have the same voicing but a different place of closure.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel where the closure happens: lips or gum ridge.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are voiced. Listen to whether the release is at the lips or on the tongue tip.
quests.explanation: "Bay" begins with the lips popping apart. "Day" begins with the tongue tip leaving the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to how the vowel ends or begins: a lower, duller edge for lips and a higher, brighter one for the tongue tip.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the release short and clean.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Front of the tongue or back of the tongue? Listen for the sharper click.
quests.explanation: The word was "tea": the tongue tip touched the ridge and released, sounding bright and sharp. "Key" releases from further back and sounds hollow.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front versus back closure, same voicing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel where the tongue touches: front or back.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is identical. Listen to the very first burst.
quests.explanation: "Call" opens with the back of the tongue lifting to the soft palate. "Tall" opens with the tip on the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a brighter click (alveolar) versus a duller pop (velar).
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip down for the velar stop.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both voiced. Compare how bright or hollow the start sounds.
quests.explanation: "Dear" starts with a crisp, bright tongue-tip release. "Gear" starts deeper and duller, from the back of the tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The alveolar stop is made with the tongue tip at the ridge behind the upper teeth; the velar stop is made with the back of the tongue at the soft palate. The velar release sounds deeper and more hollow.
quests.mouthPosition: For the alveolar stop touch the tongue tip to the ridge. For the velar stop lift the back of the tongue against the soft palate.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips or back of the tongue? Listen to the burst.
quests.explanation: It was "cool": the burst came from the back of the tongue and sounded hollow. "Pool" would pop from the lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The bilabial stop closes at the lips; the velar stop closes at the back of the tongue. The bilabial release sounds lower and fuller; the velar sounds deeper and hollow.
quests.mouthPosition: Close the lips for the bilabial; lift the back of the tongue to the soft palate for the velar.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same ending. Listen to the sound of the initial burst.
quests.explanation: "Pane" opens with a lip pop, fuller and lower. "Cane" opens with a tongue-back click.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lips versus tongue back, same voicing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel where the closure happens: lips or throat.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a burst from the lips versus one from the throat side.
quests.explanation: "Gear" releases from the back of the tongue, so the start sounds deeper. "Beer" releases from the lips, softer and rounder.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to the vowel transition: it rises into the velar and falls into the bilabial.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the release short and clean.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Words end with a hum. Do the lips close, or does the tongue tip?
quests.explanation: You heard "sun": the hum ended with the tongue tip on the ridge and the lips open. "Some" would end with the lips pressed shut.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /m/ finishes with the lips closed; /n/ finishes with the tongue tip on the ridge and the lips open. The preceding vowel also glides slightly differently.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ end with closed lips. For /n/ end with the lips open and the tongue tip touching the ridge.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the final hum: lips or tongue?
quests.explanation: "Gum" closes at the lips for a rounded ending. "Gun" ends with the tongue tip and a brighter hum.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to the nasal tail: rounded and lip-closing for /m/, bright and tongue-based for /n/.
quests.mouthPosition: Check that your lips touch for /m/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start. Which nasal hums at the end?
quests.explanation: "Ran" finishes with the tongue tip behind the teeth. "Ram" finishes with the lips closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiced nasals; place of closure is the distinction.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips relaxed for /n/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end with a nasal hum. Where does the tongue touch?
quests.explanation: "Wing" ends with the back of the tongue against the soft palate, deeper and longer. "Win" ends with the tip on the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /n/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth; /ŋ/ is made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate. Air goes through the nose for both.
quests.mouthPosition: For /n/ press the tongue tip behind the teeth. For /ŋ/ lift the back of the tongue to the soft palate and keep the tip down.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the end of the word: front hum or back hum?
quests.explanation: That was "ran": the tip of the tongue touched the ridge. "Rang" would finish with a deeper hum from the back of the mouth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue touches at the front for /n/ and at the back for /ŋ/, so the vowel before it colours differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip behind the lower teeth for /ŋ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same vowel, and a nasal ending each time. Which one sounds deeper?
quests.explanation: "Thing" ends deeper, with the back of the tongue raised. "Thin" ends brighter, with the tongue tip up.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ŋ/ sounds deeper and lasts longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Do not add a /ɡ/ after /ŋ/ in these words.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both use the lip and teeth. Which one buzzes?
quests.explanation: The word was "van": the voice buzzed during the first sound. "Fan" is a simple breathy hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /f/ and /v/ use the same lip-and-teeth position; /f/ is voiceless with strong friction, while /v/ is voiced with a softer buzz.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the upper teeth to the lower lip. Blow air for /f/; add the voice and a buzz for /v/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The word ends with lip-on-teeth friction. Buzz or hiss?
quests.explanation: "Leaf" ends with a clean hiss after a slightly shorter vowel. "Leave" gets a longer vowel and a soft buzz.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, the voiced /v/ lengthens the vowel before it and often ends weakly; /f/ shortens the vowel and finishes with a strong hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the lower lip to the upper teeth. For /f/ end with clear breathy friction; for /v/ keep the voice buzzing and hold the vowel a little longer.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two-syllable words. The difference is in the first sound only.
quests.explanation: "Very" starts with the buzz of a voiced /v/. "Ferry" starts with a hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for the hiss of /f/ compared with the buzz of /v/; the buzz makes /v/ sound weaker and darker.
quests.mouthPosition: Put a finger on your throat: it vibrates for /v/ but not for /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One starts with a hiss, the other with a buzz.
quests.explanation: "Sip" begins with a thin, silent hiss. "Zip" begins with a vibrating buzz.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /s/ is a voiceless hiss; /z/ is the same tongue shape with the voice on, producing a buzz. Listen for a clean hiss or a buzzing sound at the beginning.
quests.mouthPosition: Place the tongue tip just behind the upper teeth with a narrow groove for air. Add voice for /z/ and keep it silent for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is longer in one word. Which ending do you hear?
quests.explanation: It was "rise": the vowel lasted longer and the end had a soft buzz. "Rice" would end with a crisp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /z/ lengthens the vowel before it and has a soft buzz; /s/ shortens the vowel and ends with a crisp hiss. In final position the buzz can be weak, so vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the tongue behind the upper teeth. For /s/ end with a sharp hiss after a short vowel; for /z/ stretch the vowel and finish with a softer buzz.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two very short words. Listen for a buzz at the start.
quests.explanation: "Sue" begins with a hiss, and there is no vibration. "Zoo" begins with a buzz you could feel in your throat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue position is identical; only the voice differs. /z/ sounds heavier and buzzier than /s/.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch your throat: buzz for /z/, nothing for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end in a tongue-between-teeth sound. Voiced or voiceless? Check the vowel too.
quests.explanation: "Bathe" ends with a voiced, buzzy /ð/ after a gliding vowel. "Bath" ends with a breathy /θ/ after a long open vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ and /ð/ use the same tongue position; /θ/ is voiceless and /ð/ is voiced. The vowel before a voiced /ð/ is also longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Place the tongue tip lightly against the teeth. Blow air only for /θ/; add the voice for /ð/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: A noun and a verb that end almost the same. Listen to the length of the vowel.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "breath": a short vowel and a breathy /θ/ at the end. "Breathe" has a long vowel and a buzzing /ð/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voicing is the only difference. Put your fingers on your throat to feel it.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the throat vibrate for /ð/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Think about what the tongue does at the very end: which final sound has a buzz under it, and what happens to the vowel before it?
quests.explanation: "Clothe" has a gliding vowel and a buzzing /ð/. "Cloth" has a short vowel and a whispered /θ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The voiced version sounds heavier and buzzier.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue relaxed and the air flow soft.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two words with a middle fricative and the same ending. Buzz or hush?
quests.explanation: "Pleasure" has a buzzing /ʒ/ in the middle. "Pressure" has a voiceless /ʃ/ hush. (The /l/ and /r/ also differ, so this is a near-minimal pair.)
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is voiceless and /ʒ/ is voiced; the tongue and lip positions are identical. /ʒ/ has a soft buzz. (/ʒ/ rarely begins English words, so these pairs are near-minimal.)
quests.mouthPosition: Round the lips slightly and pull the tongue back. Blow air only for /ʃ/; add voice for /ʒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The middle sound is either voiced or voiceless.
quests.explanation: You heard "vision": the middle sound buzzed. "Fission" has a plain hush with no voice. The first sounds differ as well.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The buzz of /ʒ/ makes it softer and heavier than the crisp hush of /ʃ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the throat vibrate for /ʒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Verb or noun? The stress is the same. Listen to the ending.
quests.explanation: "Believe" ends with a soft buzz after a long vowel. "Belief" ends with a hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Final /v/ is softer and buzzier; final /f/ is sharper and ends in breath.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the throat vibrate at the end of /v/ but not /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel's length and how the word ends.
quests.explanation: The word was "bag": the vowel lingers, then the tongue closes softly. "Back" is shorter and ends with a sharp stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The clearest cue is vowel length: longer before /ɡ/, shorter before /k/.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel slightly before /ɡ/ and clip it before /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The gliding vowel is longer in one word.
quests.explanation: "Rope" ends with a sharp lip closure after a shorter vowel. "Robe" ends softly after a longer one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't wait for a burst at the end: listen to how long the vowel lasts before the lips close.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /b/ and tighten the closure for /p/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end at the tongue tip. Which one has the longer vowel?
quests.explanation: "Seed" has a longer vowel and a soft, voiced ending. "Seat" cuts the vowel short and ends with a sharp stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end on the same tongue position, but the voiced /d/ lengthens the preceding vowel while /t/ clips it.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /d/; cut it short before /t/.
